what_happened: The job was to find and remove the cause of the longer verifier stage (the stage time rose between roughly 3.1 and 3.5). The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One of 5 acceptance criteria was unmet: a note under docs/design/ (or the commit message) must state the cause of the slowdown and cite the code path or measurement that shows it. One blocker finding was listed. The cause stated in docs/design/verifier-stage-slowdown.md (Cause section) and in the CHANGELOG.md Fixed entry came after the slowdown it was meant to explain, so it cannot be the real cause of the rise from 3.1 to 3.5. No failed checks are listed.
cause: The job is a diagnose-then-fix task, and nothing requires the diagnosis to be tied to the timeline of the metric it explains. The criterion asks only that a note state a cause and cite a code path or measurement. A cause can pass that wording while being a later change, or one that does not fit when the metric moved. Athena has per-stage timing records and history, but the producer is not required to find the first jobs where the stage time rose, to list the changes that landed between the last fast job and the first slow one, or to check that the cited cause landed before the rise. The earlier rejection of the sibling checks-stage job (20261105-093606-199q) had the same defect, with a cause that did not fit the window. That finding did not become a check or a default in the request, so the same request shape was repeated for the verifier stage.
prevention: Make a metric-regression diagnosis a required, checkable result. For any job that explains a change in a measured stage time, the reading must require a timeline: the per-job stage times from the records, the last job before and the first job after the rise, and the commits that landed between them. The note must name a cause whose landing date or commit is before the first slow job, and must show a measure from the slow and fast windows (such as the verifier's input size, turns or cost per job) that moves with it. Athena should check the cited commit or date against the first slow job before dispatch to the verifier, and hand the producer a ready-made table of stage times by job and commit so the diagnosis starts from data. If no cause can be shown from the records, the note must say so and name what would settle it, and the fix part is held.
proposed_request:
Find why the verifier stage got longer, and then fix the cause. Stage times in the job records rose from about 3.1 to about 3.5 (the same measure you will read from the records). Work from the records, not from guesses.

Do this in order:
1. From the per-job stage records, list the verifier stage time for each job around the rise. Identify the last job that was fast and the first job that was slow, and list the commits that landed between them (include merges to main and changes to athena.toml, prompts and the verifier code).
2. State the cause in a note under docs/design/ (name it verifier-stage-slowdown.md). The note must name a specific commit or change that landed at or before the first slow job, cite the code path in crates/ or the config or prompt line that it changed, and give a measure from jobs before and after (for example verifier turns, tokens read, cost or time per job) that shows the change explains the rise. A cause that landed after the rise does not count. If the records do not show a cause, say that, say what is missing, and do not make a code change.
3. If a cause is shown, remove it with the smallest change that restores the earlier verifier time without dropping any check the verifier ran before. Add a CHANGELOG.md Fixed entry that states only what the diff does.

Acceptance:
- The note contains a timeline table of verifier stage times by job with the fast-to-slow boundary marked, and the cited cause lands before that boundary.
- The note cites a measure from both windows that moves with the cause.
- The fix, if any, touches only the code path or config the note names, and the CHANGELOG entry matches the diff.
- Existing tests and checks pass.
